title: Power Badge
statement: A coding site gives a badge to players whose score is a power of two (1, 2, 4, 8, ...). Return true if `score` is a power of two. Try to answer without a loop.

answerKey.pattern: A power of two has exactly one 1 bit: n > 0 and n & (n - 1) === 0
keyPoints: Powers of two in binary are a single 1 followed by zeros
n & (n - 1) clears the lowest 1 bit, which leaves 0 only when there was one 1 bit
Zero and negative numbers are not powers of two
edgeCases: 2^30, the largest power of two that fits
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Divide by 2 while even and check the result is 1: O(log n)

hints: Write 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 in binary. What do they have in common?
Each has exactly one 1 bit. Which expression clears the lowest 1 bit?
